title: HIS-201 Ch. 7 — 3 Numbers & Dates
subject: HIS-201
topic: Chapter 7: The American People and the American Revolution, 1775-1783

cards.def: On June 17, 1775, 1,600 rebels held Breed's Hill until their ammunition ran out, costing Britain 228 dead and 800 wounded.

cards.term: When the Second Continental Congress met
cards.def: It met on May 10, 1775, a month after Lexington and Concord.

cards.term: When the Olive Branch Petition was sent

cards.def: Dunmore offered freedom to slaves in November 1775.
Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.
Perhaps one-fifth of the population backed the king in 1775.
At its peak Britain had 50,000 troops plus about 30,000 Hessians.

cards.term: When Trenton and Princeton were fought
cards.def: Washington took Trenton on Christmas night 1776 and won at Princeton on January 3, 1777.

cards.term: When France allied with the US
cards.def: France signed its alliance in early 1778, Spain joined less than a year later, and Britain was fighting the Dutch by 1780.
About 2,500 of 11,000 soldiers died at Valley Forge in winter 1777-78.
Charleston surrendered to the British on May 12, 1780.

cards.term: When King's Mountain and Cowpens were fought
cards.def: King's Mountain came in October 1780 and Cowpens in January 1781.

cards.term: When the Treaty of Paris was signed
cards.def: The Treaty of Paris was signed on September 3, 1783.
